Concurrency in the estate is declared data: a capability's envelope carries an
`executionGraph`, `analysis.capability_graph_source` copies six keys onto the
graph source, and the kernel compiler turns them into a plan. One scenario
with sequential operations compiles to `edge:sequence`; independent branches
exist only when the declaration says so.

## 1. The envelope shape (proven, four-branch circuit)

`$.semantics.executionGraph`:

```json
{ "graphType": "sda-semantic-execution-graph.v2",
  "requiredExecutionFeatures": ["declared-concurrent-dispatch.v1"],
  "readyArbitration": "causal-activation-order.v1",
  "executionBudget": { "maximumInFlightEffects": N, "deadlineMs": 60000 },
  "dispatchAuthorities": [ { "dispatchAuthorityId": "circuit-dispatch.v1",
    "mode": "concurrent", "legCount": N, "maximumActiveBranches": N,
    "maximumInFlightEffects": N, "readyOrder": "declared-edge-order",
    "branchFailure": "collect", "ownership": "join-before-return" } ],
  "edgeGroups": [
    { "groupId": "circuit-fan", "kind": "broadcast", "policy": "all",
      "edgeIds": ["edge:enter-<leg>", ...],
      "dispatchAuthorityId": "circuit-dispatch.v1",
      "completionJoinGroupId": "circuit-converge" },
    { "groupId": "circuit-converge", "kind": "join", "policy": "all-required",
      "edgeIds": ["edge:settle-<leg>", ...],
      "joinCellId": "cell:scenario:<assessment-scenario>",
      "requiredSlotIds": ["<leg>", ...] } ] }
```

Routing transitions (`$.semantics.routing`, consumed by
`analysis.capability_declared_transitions`) carry `topologyKind`
(`broadcast` | `join` | `failure` | `sequence`), `groupId` and `joinSlotId`.
Rule of thumb: three transitions per leg - `enter-<leg>` (broadcast),
`settle-<leg>` (join, named slot), `fail-<leg>` (failure, same slot).

## 2. Re-mint, don't patch

The envelope is content-addressed. Change it by loading the current envelope,
`JSON_MODIFY`-ing `$.semantics.cli|routing|executionGraph`, minting the new
definition and capability version (the pattern in
`complete-financial-branch-fanout.sql`), then re-declaring unchanged scenarios.
Probe the graph source afterwards: graphType v2, `mode` concurrent,
`maximumActiveBranches` N, transitions = 3N, fan edges N, join slots N.

## 3. The serial/concurrent distinction

- Serial: no `executionGraph` on the envelope; events show `edge:sequence`
  between all cells with disjoint `[startedAt, completedAt]` windows.
- Concurrent: branch cells' windows **overlap** (both start before either
  completes - the slow branch is the barrier) and the join cell starts after
  all required settlements.
- The demo rig: `demo/dispatch-pair/` (`fixture-server.mjs` provides the 400ms
  barrier; `observation-capture.v1.txt` documents the capture shape).
  `dispatch-pair-demo` switches M1 serial / M2 concurrent by re-minting one
  declared value; input contract requires `{contractId, payload:{symbol}}` when
  the catalog is healthy.
- Witness discipline: retain both runs; read the timelines (events or the
  rig's capture); assert overlap programmatically. A missing or empty events
  page is not proof of absence - read the run output contract as well.

## 4. The admission/catalog dependency

Live invocation refuses `CAPABILITY_INPUT_JSON_REJECTED` when the catalog's
contract schema diverges from the caller's input. The catalog resolves through
scenario contract version pins; repairs follow the `derived-surface-repair`
skill (scaffold residue and pin staleness are the usual causes).

## 5. The DSL emission target

`analysis.compile_capability_dsl` compiles the line-oriented DSL into the
capability document. The emission unit (`dsl-fanout-construct`) adds a
construct for fan-out/dependency + join that emits `edgeGroups`,
`dispatchAuthorities` and the routing transitions above, so the lane authors
concurrent topology from text (`sfx capability author --dsl`). Read the
compiler's construct mechanics first and size the unit before promising it -
constructs may be table-driven or hardcoded. Keep serial and
dependency-ordered (`sequence`) paths expressible; add a conformance vector.
